docs.title: Renovate: weekly grouped updates with gated automerge
docs.text:
Status: implemented (see ADR 0001). The config below is the proposal; renovate.json is the source of truth, and it adds a Task version pin and an extractVersion rule.

Mirror what tangle already ships (tangle ADR 0013, ADR 0016): a weekly schedule, one PR per ecosystem, a 5-day minimumReleaseAge, and automerge for everything except majors in the primary language.

docs.title: How tangle does it (reference)
docs.text:
• "schedule": ["on friday"], minimumReleaseAge: "5 days" with minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour: "timestamp-optional".
  • Ecosystem groups (go, ts, k8s, ci) built from matchDatasources/matchManagers, with each language's Dockerfile base images (golang, node) pulled into the same group by matchPackageNames.
  • Automerge for minor/patch/pin/digest everywhere, and for majors everywhere except Go and TypeScript (ADR 0016).
  • Version caps with a description saying when to drop them (typescript <7).
  • customManagers regex entries for pins Renovate can't otherwise see.
  • renovate-config-validator in pre-commit (rubrical already has this).

docs.title: Why rubrical's PRs pile up
docs.text:
There are only three Renovate PRs open right now (#523, #532, #541), but none of them will merge on its own:

PR Update State Cause #523 docker/metadata-action v5 → v6 all green, not merged repo has allow_auto_merge: false and main has no branch protection, so platformAutomerge can't do anything. Renovate falls back to merging the PR itself on a later run, and with a biweekly schedule that run is a long way off. #532 actions/setup-python v6 → v7 main fails arduino/setup-task hit the unauthenticated GitHub API rate limit. This is a flake, not a v7 break. #541 Python 3.14 → 3.15 (.python-version) main + docker fail cffi==2.0.0 has no 3.15 wheel and the DHI image has no cc. Renovate calls this a minor bump, so if CI had passed, today's blanket automerge: true would have moved the runtime with nobody looking.

Two other problems:

  • The Dependency Dashboard (#5) warns Failed to look up docker package dhi.io/python: no-result. Docker Hardened Images need auth, so the Dockerfile base image is never updated.
  • Some pins are invisible to Renovate or float: ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:debian in Dockerfile has no version, and octocov's version: v0.79.0 in ci.yaml isn't tracked.

docs.title: 1. Fix CI so bot PRs can go green
docs.text:
Pass the workflow token to arduino/setup-task in ci.yaml, release.yaml, and release-docs.yaml:

      - name: Install Task
        uses: arduino/setup-task@v3.0.0
        with:
          repo-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

Why the token: with no version: input the action defaults to 3.x, and it lists Task's releases through the GitHub REST API to turn that range into a real version. Without repo-token the call is unauthenticated, which limits it to 60 requests/hour per IP, and GitHub-hosted runners share IPs. With the workflow token the limit is per repo (about 1,000/hour). The token is already there in every run, Renovate branches included, and contents: read is enough.

Also pin an exact Task version (version: 3.54.0). When the input is valid semver, computeVersion in the action skips the API lookup, and the pin gives Renovate something to bump. Leave the v off: semver.valid accepts v3.54.0, and the action prepends its own v, which gives vv3.54.0.

docs.title: 2. Repo settings (manual, GitHub UI)
docs.text:
• Turn on Allow auto-merge (Settings → General).
  • Add a ruleset on main that requires the main, docker, and pre-commit checks. Without required checks, GitHub auto-merge has nothing to wait for. With them in place, platformAutomerge merges as soon as CI passes, and doesn't need another Renovate run.
  • Add yourself (repo admin) as a bypass actor on the ruleset, or every change to main has to go through a PR from now on.

docs.title: 3. Restructure renovate.json
docs.text:
Groups:

  • python: pep621 (pyproject and uv.lock), the pyenv runtime (.python-version), the Dockerfile base images (dhi.io/python, ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv), and the devcontainer's ghcr.io/ivanklee86/devcontainer/python image. All of these must move together on a runtime bump, which is why the devcontainer image goes here and not in the devcontainer group.
  • ci: the github-actions manager (this already covers prek-version) plus the new octocov custom manager (custom.regex).
  • devcontainer dependencies: kept as it is (features only, after the python image moves out), automerged.
  • Weekly lockFileMaintenance, so uv.lock picks up transitive bumps. It stays in its own renovate/lock-file-maintenance PR: Renovate doesn't merge lock file maintenance into other groups, and keeping it separate means a bad transitive bump can't hold up direct-dependency updates. The >= ranges in pyproject.toml mean most direct-dependency updates come through as lockfile-only changes too.

Python runtime cap: cap the runtime at <3.15 (in the same style as tangle's typescript <7 rule) until 3.15 is a deliberate change. That change also has to bump requires-python and the DHI and devcontainer tags, and it waits on 3.15 wheels.

Automerge: put every non-major update on automerge, and majors too, except in the python group (tangle ADR 0016's pattern applied to Python). Drop the top-level automerge: true and platformAutomerge: true: the rules now cover automerge, and platformAutomerge is already Renovate's default.

A grouped branch only automerges if every update in it can automerge, so a single Python major holds the whole python PR. That's intended. separateMajorMinor (on by default) puts majors in their own python (major) PR, so the non-major python PR still automerges.

{
  "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  "extends": ["config:recommended"],
  "schedule": ["on friday"],
  "minimumReleaseAge": "5 days",
  "minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour": "timestamp-optional",
  "lockFileMaintenance": {
    "enabled": true,
    "schedule": ["on friday"]
  },
  "hostRules": [
    {
      "matchHost": "dhi.io",
      "username": "ivanklee86",
      "password": "{{ secrets.DHI_TOKEN }}"
    }
  ],
  "packageRules": [
    {
      "matchManagers": ["pep621", "pyenv"],
      "groupName": "python"
    },
    {
      "matchManagers": ["dockerfile"],
      "matchPackageNames": ["dhi.io/python", "ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv"],
      "groupName": "python"
    },
    {
      "matchManagers": ["devcontainer"],
      "matchPackageNames": ["ghcr.io/ivanklee86/devcontainer/python"],
      "groupName": "python"
    },
    {
      "description": "Python 3.15 is a deliberate bump (requires-python, DHI + devcontainer tags, wheels for cffi et al.); drop when moving",
      "matchPackageNames": ["python", "dhi.io/python", "ghcr.io/ivanklee86/devcontainer/python"],
      "allowedVersions": "<3.15"
    },
    {
      "matchManagers": ["github-actions", "custom.regex"],
      "groupName": "ci"
    },
    {
      "matchManagers": ["devcontainer"],
      "matchPackageNames": ["!ghcr.io/ivanklee86/devcontainer/python"],
      "groupName": "devcontainer dependencies"
    },
    {
      "matchUpdateTypes": ["minor", "patch", "pin", "digest", "lockFileMaintenance", "major"],
      "automerge": true
    },
    {
      "matchManagers": ["pep621", "pyenv"],
      "matchUpdateTypes": ["major"],
      "automerge": false
    },
    {
      "matchPackageNames": ["dhi.io/python", "ghcr.io/ivanklee86/devcontainer/python"],
      "matchUpdateTypes": ["major"],
      "automerge": false
    }
  ],
  "customManagers": [
    {
      "customType": "regex",
      "managerFilePatterns": ["/^\\.github/workflows/ci\\.yaml$/"],
      "matchStrings": ["version: (?<currentValue>v[0-9.]+) # (?<datasource>.*?)/(?<depName>.*?)\\s"]
    }
  ]
}

Supporting file changes:

  • ci.yaml: annotate the octocov pin as version: v0.79.0 # github-releases/k1LoW/octocov, the same convention tangle uses for K3D_VERSION.
  • Dockerfile: pin ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:debian to 0.13.5-debian@sha256:…. That's the current release, which :debian was already pulling, so behavior doesn't change. The pin gives Renovate a tag and a digest to bump.
  • ci.yaml, release.yaml, release-docs.yaml: the exact Task version: from step 1, annotated # github-releases/go-task/task. The custom manager matches all workflows and accepts an optional v, and a go-task/task rule sets extractVersion: "^v(?<version>.*)$" so Renovate writes back bare versions.

docs.title: 4. Credentials for dhi.io
docs.text: Add a DHI_TOKEN secret (a Docker Hub PAT with DHI pull access) for this repo in the Mend developer portal, then use the hostRules entry above. If that's more than we want to maintain, use {"matchPackageNames": ["dhi.io/python"], "enabled": false} instead. This makes the "manual only" choice explicit and removes the dashboard warning. If you take that route, also take dhi.io/python out of the python group rule, the major-automerge exclusion, and the <3.15 cap, and drop the hostRules block, so no dead config is left behind.

docs.title: 532: once step 1 lands, rebase it from the dashboard and let it automerge. It will reopen as part of the ci group.
541: close it. The <3.15 cap stops it from coming back.
519 (pre-commit.ci autoupdate) isn't from Renovate, and tangle ADR 0013 deliberately leaves rev: bumps to
docs.text: pre-commit.ci. Look at it separately.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• prek run renovate-config-validator --all-files passes.
  • After the next Friday run, the Dependency Dashboard shows at most one PR each for python, ci, and devcontainer dependencies (plus python (major) if one is pending), and a separate lock file maintenance PR. It no longer shows the dhi.io lookup warning, and it lists k1LoW/octocov and ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv under detected dependencies.
  • Check that a non-major ci PR automerges without anyone touching it once the required checks pass.

docs.title: 6. Record it as an ADR
docs.text: Create docs/adrs/ and add ADR 0001 covering the weekly grouped schedule, the <3.15 runtime cap, and keeping Python majors out of automerge. Tangle recorded this as ADR 0013 plus 0016. Without an ADR, the cap and the exclusion look arbitrary to the next reader.

docs.title: Resolved questions
docs.text:
• Lock file maintenance gets its own PR (see step 3).
  • Yes, add an ADR (step 6).

docs.title: Replace Codecov with octocov and the central tracking repo
docs.text:
Status: implemented. rubrical PR 1 (steps 1–4), octocov-central (step 5), and rubrical PR 2 (the README badge) are done. Step 6 (removing the Codecov secret and app) is manual and remains. Open decisions resolved: octocov v0.79.0 supports patch in coverage.acceptable, so the 85% patch gate is kept (current >= 90% && diff >= -0.5% && patch >= 85%); octocov dump report confirmed repo-relative rubrical/... paths.

Mirror what tangle already ships (tangle ADR 0010, ADR 0011): octocov posts PR coverage diffs using the workflow's own GITHUB_TOKEN and an artifact:// datastore, and ivanklee86/octocov-central collects those artifacts daily and publishes a public badge.

rubrical is simpler than tangle: one test job and one coverage file, so no separate report job and no coverage merging.

docs.title: How tangle does it (reference)
docs.text:
• tangle CI uploads raw coverage profiles as artifacts. A report job runs k1LoW/octocov-action (SHA-pinned, binary pinned to v0.79.0) with actions: write for the artifact://${GITHUB_REPOSITORY} datastore. It stores reports on main, and on PRs it diffs against main and comments.
  • octocov-central runs octocov in central mode on a daily cron, reading artifact://ivanklee86/tangle with the TANGLE_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN PAT and writing badges/<owner>/<repo>/*.svg. Its .octocov.yml omits central.push, because octocov's own go-git push never authenticated, and the workflow commits and pushes with plain git instead.

docs.title: 1. Emit LCOV from pytest
docs.text:
In tasks/python.yaml test-cov, add (or swap the XML report for) --cov-report lcov:test_results/cov.lcov.

coverage.py's Cobertura XML uses an absolute <source> plus filenames relative to it, and octocov's path handling for that is unverified. coverage.py's LCOV writes repo-relative SF:rubrical/... paths, which is the safer choice. Verify with octocov dump report that the file paths come out repo-relative. This needs the devcontainer, since .venv only works there.

docs.title: 2. Add .octocov.yml
docs.text:
coverage:
  paths:
    - test_results/cov.lcov
  # Rough equivalent of codecov.yaml's project target 90% / threshold 0.5%.
  acceptable: current >= 90% && diff >= -0.5%
report:
  datastores:
    - artifact://${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}
  if: is_default_branch
diff:
  datastores:
    - artifact://${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}
  if: is_pull_request
comment:
  if: is_pull_request

Open decisions:

  • codecov.yaml also has a patch gate (85% target), but I don't know of a direct octocov equivalent. Check the octocov docs, or accept dropping it.
  • The acceptable expression syntax is from memory. Check it against octocov v0.79.0.
  • tangle sets no gate at all, so keeping one here is a deliberate difference.

docs.title: 3. Update .github/workflows/ci.yaml
docs.text:
• Add a job-level permissions: block to main: contents: read, pull-requests: write, actions: write. The workflow has none today, so it relies on the repo's default token permissions.
  • Replace codecov/codecov-action@v6 with:
- name: Report coverage via octocov
  # SHA-pinned rather than the mutable tag: this step runs with actions: write.
  uses: k1LoW/octocov-action@a167dc0dee441b7ffc45e1b862ab55ec0d87f278 # v1.5.2
  with:
    config: .octocov.yml
    version: v0.79.0
  • Keep it running only when tests pass, as Codecov does now, so a failed run never becomes the base other PRs diff against.
  • Known limitation: on PRs from forks the token is read-only, so the comment step fails. tangle has the same problem. It matters little here because most of rubrical's PRs are same-repo Renovate branches.

docs.title: 4. Clean up in rubrical
docs.text:
• Delete codecov.yaml.
  • Mention octocov in docs/development.md, and optionally in docs/agents/internals.md.
  • In a follow-up PR, after step 5 has produced the badge: replace the Codecov badge in README.md with https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ivanklee86/octocov-central/main/badges/ivanklee86/rubrical/coverage.svg (link target: match whatever tangle's README uses).

docs.title: 5. Changes in octocov-central
docs.text:
• Add - artifact://ivanklee86/rubrical under central.reports.datastores in .octocov.yml.
  • Manual (GitHub UI): edit the fine-grained PAT to also grant read-only Actions access on ivanklee86/rubrical. Central mode uses a single OCTOCOV_GITHUB_TOKEN for every source.
  • Optionally save it under a generic secret name, such as OCTOCOV_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN, and update .github/workflows/central.yaml to use it. TANGLE_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN no longer describes what it's for.
  • Once rubrical's main has completed one CI run, trigger central.yaml via workflow_dispatch and confirm badges/ivanklee86/rubrical/coverage.svg appears.

docs.title: 6. Manual cleanup after merge
docs.text:
• Remove the CODECOV_TOKEN secret if there is one, and the Codecov app or project for rubrical.
  • Codecov's historical data does not carry over.

docs.title: Order of work
docs.text:
1. rubrical PR 1: steps 1–3, plus deleting codecov.yaml and updating the docs. Merge to main.
  2. octocov-central: step 5.
  3. rubrical PR 2: the README badge.
  4. Optional tangle PR: the cleanups below.

docs.title: Side findings from reviewing tangle's implementation
docs.text:
Minor, nothing broken:

  • docs/agents/ci.md ("Mostly done" bullet) and workstream 11 step 6 in docs/agents/plans/ci-pipeline-restructure.md still say the badge isn't added. It is, and it renders.
  • ADRs 0010 and 0011 are still status: "proposed", though both are implemented.
  • ADR 0011 rejects octocov.dev and plans a Pages URL, but the README badge links to octocov.dev and loads the image from raw.githubusercontent.com. Either update the ADR or change the link.
  • octocov-central's central.yaml uses actions/checkout@v4 by tag and downloads the octocov tarball without checking its checksum, while holding a token that reaches other repos. That's a lower bar than tangle's own SHA-pinned CI.
